arm-01.note: payment-reminders cron reminds every FINALIZED order with an open balance, deduped per order per calendar day via the idempotency key; a separate pickup-expiry cron stamps overdue ready pickups as expired and notifies.

arm-03.note: runPaymentReminderCron() reminds PLACED/PAID orders with UNPAID/PARTIAL status, day-deduped via idempotencyBase; runPickupExpiryCron() is a separate, correctly-scoped sweep — both logged to CronRunLog.

arm-04.note: Configurable-cadence payment-reminder sweep keyed off a followUpDays setting, plus a separate pickup-expiry sweep — solid, though not clearly ahead of the clone cluster's own cadence logic.

arm-05.note: sendPaymentReminders() is mis-scoped: it only reminds customers with a bulkDeliverySchedule whose order.paymentStatus === PENDING, missing general unpaid finalized orders entirely (a materially narrower cron than the name implies). Pickup expiry (expirePickupPackages) is a separate, correct sweep.

arm-06.note: sweepPaymentReminders() with a configurable cadence (first reminder after initialAfterDays, then every intervalDays via lastPaymentReminderAt) plus a CronRun audit row per run; sweepPickupExpiry() runs a readiness sync before the expiry pass — most sophisticated cadence of the six.

arm-01.note: planShipment(): genuine first-fit-decreasing bin packing with real per-axis dimension checks and per-box running volume/weight capacity (not a scalar volume sum), plus a full carrier integration (quote/buy/void label, refresh tracking, validate address) — the most complete shipping stack of the six, though it hard-throws when nothing fits.

arm-03.note: packItems(): real per-axis first-fit-decreasing bin packing with running volume/weight capacity per box, and gracefully reports unpackedItemIds instead of throwing when nothing fits.

arm-04.note: planParcels() is a scalar volume/weight-sum selector — its own code comment admits "Volume and weight, not a three-dimensional fit" — with zero per-axis dimension checks; this is the exact flaw that disqualified arm-05 on this same item, directly contradicting the prior (wrong) grading of 8.

arm-05.note: parcelForPackage() sums ALL product volumes into one scalar and picks the smallest PackageType whose box volume >= that sum — no per-axis dimension check, no multi-box split, exactly one ShipmentBox per package always. Arm-05's own AGGREGATE-REVIEW-P8.md independently confirms: "'Bin packing' is a single-box volume-sum selection, not bin packing."

arm-06.note: planParcels(): best-fit-decreasing multi-parcel packing (smallest-fitting-open-parcel search, 85% fill ratio) — arguably a better placement heuristic than first-fit — but throws a hard DomainRuleError on an item that fits no configured box instead of gracefully shipping it as its own parcel.

evidence.arm-04: lib/shipping/bin-packing.ts (planParcels — self-documented scalar volume-sum, not per-axis)
